Article Title: QR code, no queue: 25 crore OPD registrations go digital
Article Text:
Long wait at hospital registration counters is slowly giving way to a QR code

NEW DELHI: The long wait at hospital registration counters is slowly giving way to a QR code. In a sign of India's growing digital health footprint, patients have now completed 25 crore outpatient (OPD) registrations through the ABHA-based 'Scan and Register' service under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), with nearly four lakh people using the facility every day.Introduced in October 2022, the service allows patients to register for an OPD consultation by simply scanning a QR code displayed at participating hospitals through an ABDM-enabled health app. Once they give consent, their ABHA-linked details are shared with the hospital, eliminating paperwork and reducing waiting time at registration counters.The service is now available in 30,800 hospitals and healthcare facilities across 36 states and Union Territories and 756 districts, making it one of the country's fastest-growing digital public health services. More than 24,000 government facilities and 6,400 private hospitals have adopted the system.The biggest users of the platform are in Bihar, which has recorded over 7.3 crore digital OPD registrations, followed by Uttar Pradesh (4.09 crore), Andhra Pradesh (3.38 crore) and Jammu & Kashmir (1.39 crore).Among hospitals, AIIMS New Delhi has emerged as the country's busiest digital registration centre, recording over 54.29 lakh Scan and Register transactions.It is followed by AIIMS Bhopal (29.1 lakh), AIIMS Bhubaneswar (23.93 lakh), AIIMS Patna (19.62 lakh) and AIIMS Raipur (18.63 lakh).Officials said the service has particularly eased hospital visits for senior citizens, pregnant women and patients requiring frequent follow-ups by cutting time spent at registration counters and doing away with repeated form filling."This milestone reflects the growing trust that citizens and healthcare providers have placed in India's digital health ecosystem. By simplifying one of the most common touchpoints in healthcare, OPD registration, the service has enhanced patient convenience while improving efficiency for hospitals," National Health Authority CEO Dr Sunil Kumar Barnwal said.The National Health Authority said the service is now operational across AIIMS, central and state government hospitals, medical colleges, district hospitals, ESIC and railway hospitals, as well as private healthcare facilities, and is expected to expand further as more hospitals adopt ABHA-enabled digital services.
Article Summary: Patients have now completed 25 crore outpatient (OPD) registrations through the ABHA-based 'Scan and Register' service under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. Nearly four lakh people use the facility every day. More than 24,000 government facilities and 6,400 private hospitals have adopted the system.

Article Title: Akal Takht panel asks Punjab govt to address objections before anti-sacrilege talks
Article Text:
Akal Takht panel flags Punjab govt response, seeks compliance report on anti-sacrilege law

NEW DELHI: The expert panel appointed by the Akal Takht on Friday asked the Punjab government to first submit a compliance report on the objections raised by the Sikh temporal seat before any further talks on the proposed anti-sacrilege law.The panel, formed to discuss the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 with the state government, held its first meeting on Thursday.The panel said the Punjab government's July 29 response did not address the main concerns raised by the Akal Takht, especially those related to possible interference in Sikh religious matters.On June 29, Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj had given the state government one month to respond to his objections to the anti-sacrilege law.In a statement on Friday, the Akal Takht secretariat said the government's response, submitted just before the deadline, was an attempt to avoid the main issues. It said the concerns of the Sikh community had already been conveyed to the Punjab assembly Speaker and members of the state Cabinet on July 31.The secretariat also accused the Bhagwant Mann-led government of not taking a constructive approach towards resolving the sensitive issue.It said that despite being given enough time, the Punjab government had not formed its own panel to discuss the matter.Earlier, Jathedar Gargajj had rejected the government's response as "unsatisfactory" and announced a five-member expert panel to hold discussions with the Aam Aadmi Party government.The panel includes retired judges Rupinder Singh Sodhi and Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, and Sikh scholars Dr Kehar Singh and Prof Jagmohan Singh.The Jathedar had also written to Punjab assembly Speaker Kultar Singh, Sikh MLAs and state ministers, asking them not to discuss or amend the anti-sacrilege law without a wider "Panthic" consensus.He had directed Sikh MLAs and Cabinet ministers to ensure that no discussion on the law takes place during the assembly session that began on August 3 until an agreement is reached with the Akal Takht and the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC).The issue came up after AAP MLA Inderbir Singh Nijjar submitted the Punjab government's response to the objections raised by the Akal Takht over the proposed anti-sacrilege legislation.
Article Summary: The panel said the Punjab government's July 29 response did not address the main concerns raised by the Akal Takht. The panel, formed to discuss the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 with the state government, held its first meeting on Thursday.

Article Title: 17.4 lakh blood components discarded in 2025 despite record collection
Article Text:
India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025, even as blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, according to state-wise data tabled in the Rajya Sabha, highlighting continued challenges in blood inventory management despite a steady rise in donations.Available official data indicate that China and India are among the world's largest blood collection programmes. In 2025, India collected 15.71 million units of blood, while China collected 25.5 million units, according to China's National Health Commission.The data, reported by blood centres through the government's e-Raktakosh portal, show that expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood components, followed by reactive units and other operational reasons. Reason-wise discard data has been captured on the portal since 2024, while such details were not available for 2023.Replying to a question in Parliament, the Union health ministry, however, said it had not received any report of regional blood shortages. It added that ensuring an adequate supply of safe blood and minimising wastage is primarily the responsibility of state governments and Union Territories, while the Centre advocates a hub-and-spoke model under which blood is collected and processed at high-volume centres before being distributed to smaller blood banks and storage centres.According to the data, Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest blood collection in 2025 with 21.6 lakh units, followed by Maharashtra (18.73 lakh), Gujarat (11.82 lakh), Rajasthan (10.79 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (9.74 lakh). Overall blood collection increased from 1.42 crore units in 2023 to 1.58 crore units in 2025.The annexure also showed a corresponding increase in blood component utilisation, with Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan reporting the highest utilisation during 2025.At the same time, Uttar Pradesh reported the highest discard of blood components at 2.40 lakh, followed by Maharashtra (1.87 lakh), Kerala (1.44 lakh), Rajasthan (1.21 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (1.09 lakh). The ministry did not provide an analysis of the wide variation in discard across states.Dr Hema Goyal, Consultant (Blood centre & Lab services), Aakash healthcare said blood wastage is inevitable to some extent, particularly because platelets have a shelf life of only five days. But discarding 17.4 lakh blood components in a year points to a mismatch between collection and actual demand. The solution is not fewer donations but smarter inventory management through real-time stock sharing and better coordination between blood banks.
Article Summary: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025. Blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, according to state-wise data tabled in the Rajya Sabha. Expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood, followed by reactive units.

Article Title: FSSAI pulls up two popular food products over safety, compliance lapses
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a fresh crackdown on food safety violations, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has acted against two food products, penalising the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard and stopping the sale of a Monk Fruit Sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.The regulator imposed a penalty on AWL Agri Business Ltd, Mangaluru, after a laboratory analysis of a retail sample of Fortune "Fryola" Refined Sunflower Seed Oil found that its vitamin D content was below the prescribed standard, making the fortified edible oil substandard under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said the company was given an opportunity to present its case, but the adjudicating authority concluded that it had manufactured and marketed a substandard fortified edible oil before imposing a monetary penalty.In a separate action, the regulator prohibited the sale of PIE Foods' Monk Fruit Sweetener, a natural zero-calorie sugar substitute, after inspections found cartons of the product stored at the company's premises without the required manufacturing licence.FSSAI also alleged that the product carried claims such as "100% Monk Fruit Extract" and "Natural Ingredients", while its online listing did not carry the mandatory endorsement required under food safety regulations.It further said the company failed to produce records showing that the monk fruit extract used in the product had been procured in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act.The prohibition order will remain in force until the product complies with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and related regulations.The regulator said the actions are part of its ongoing drive to tighten enforcement against food business operators and ensure that products sold to consumers meet prescribed safety and quality standards.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has acted against two food products. The regulator penalised the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard. It also stopped the sale of a Monk Fruit Sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.

Article Title: Om Birla seeks proposal for Makar Dwar porch
Article Text:
Officials said this is necessary considering that MPs arriving and leaving the new Parliament House wait for their vehicles out in the open

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has asked CPWD officials and its architects to consider the feasibility and submit a proposal for the construction of a porch at Makar Dwar, which is mostly used by members of Parliament to enter and exit the complex.The plan of the porch would address the inconvenience caused to MPs and other staff, particularly when it rains.At present, the entrance is uncovered, unlike other “dwars” that the Speaker, Rajya Sabha chairman and PM use. Central Public Works Department (CPWD) will carry out a feasibility exercise to add a porch over this entrance. Officials said this is necessary considering that MPs arriving and leaving the new Parliament House wait for their vehicles out in the open. The government has not yet disclosed the exact cost of the project, which has reportedly escalated to around Rs 1,300 crore.

Article Title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
Article Text:
The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Thursday passed a Bill that seeks to ease tax rules to attract investments and remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on notified electronic payment modes.The Bill — passed without discussion amid din — also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act and give legal backing to the government to modify the zero-MDR framework on UPI and RuPay card transactions. Outside the House, however, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. Ramesh said the Bill opens the doors for MDR. The FM responded, saying the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation.“More importantly, the UPI and services steering committee headed by NPCI is yet to decide on the MDR. This will happen after Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026... All this could have been discussed on the floor of the House if your party @INCIndia (Congress) engages constructively in Parliament when the Bill was/is tabled,” she said.While leaving person-to-payments outside MDR’s ambit, banks and fintechs may be permitted to charge 0.25% to 0.4% on payments to businesses in excess of Rs 2,000 with an overall ceiling on how much can be charged.Officials have argued that the levy will be lower than what is charged on credit and debit cards, and most merchants will not pass it on to consumers.
Article Summary: The Bill also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act. Outside the House, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users.

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhand’s largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee."Congress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms."We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site."He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.
Article Summary: Protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday. Students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. Political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified. 11-member delegation finalised for talks with the state government.

Article Title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
Article Text:
Aule On-screen setup running multibody dynamics simulations and tracking system capturing hardware test data for position and velocity for correlation

Aule 2: Dark room hardware test setup where the team recreated on-orbit lighting conditions with a sun simulator and a target mounted on a robotic arm to simulate the target’s motion.

BENGALURU: What if satellites could simply plug into a power bank instead of drifting away when they run out of fuel? That’s the idea driving a Bengaluru startup building “jetpack” satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft, take over their propulsion duties and keep billion-dollar assets working years longer.After recently validating a key part of its technology at an Isro facility used for India’s SpaDeX docking mission, Aule Space is now preparing for what could become one of the world’s most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations.For satellite operators, running out of fuel doesn’t necessarily mean spacecraft have reached the end of life. In many cases, expensive communication satellites remain fully functional, but can no longer maintain their assigned orbital positions because they have exhausted the propellant needed for station-keeping. Once that happens, operators are forced to retire assets worth hundreds of millions of dollars.Aule has found another way. “We’re trying to build satellites which can go and dock to existing satellites in space which don’t have any installed ports... and extend their life so that they can keep generating revenue,” CEO Jay Panchal, told TOI. “It’s like a power bank,” he added.Instead of attempting the far more complicated task of refuelling satellites in orbit, Aule’s approach is to send a smaller “jetpack” spacecraft that docks with an existing communications satellite and assumes responsibility for station-keeping using its own propulsion system.The company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build and generate significant annual revenues.The challenge lies in docking with satellites that were never designed to be serviced. Rather than relying on dedicated docking ports, Aule will attach its spacecraft to the liquid apogee motor (LAM) nozzle, a standard external feature found on most geostationary satellites.If successful, the technology could help operators extract years of additional service from satellites that would otherwise become orbital relics. Panchal said each docked “jetpack” could extend a satellite’s operational life by up to 5 years.*Key Test Done*The startup recently completed a major milestone by testing its camera-based guidance, navigation and control system at the Rendezvous Simulation Laboratory (RSL) at Isro’s ISITE — the same lab where critical elements of the SpaDeX were validated.“We were the first non-govt entity to access RSL. This is the best kind of on-ground testing we can do for these capabilities,” Panchal said.One of Aule’s differentiators is its reliance on computer vision instead of multiple specialised sensors. Current docking systems typically use LiDAR, infrared cameras and other sensors. Aule says its spacecraft will perform the critical final approach using a single optical camera powered by onboard AI.The visual navigation models are trained using data generated in its own facilities and validated at Isro’s testbed before being deployed in orbit.The company is targeting an in-orbit demonstration next year, when it plans to launch two satellites that will autonomously dock in low-Earth orbit. Panchal claims it could be the world’s first private mission to perform non-cooperative docking in LEO using camera-only navigation. The mission will validate technologies that Aule ultimately intends to deploy around geostationary communication satellites.
Article Summary: Bengaluru startup building ‘jetpack’ satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft. Aule Space preparing for what could become one of the world’s most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations. Company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build.

"Being apolitical, it gives voice to the voiceless," he said, adding that this had been his advice to its leadership.

Article Title: Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment in 2013 rape case; gets two weeks to surrender
Article Text:
Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PANAJI: Thirteen years after the arrest of a high profile editor-in-chief of Tehelka magazine, Tarun Tejpal , for rape in an elevator of a starred hotel, the Bombay high court on Thursday found him guilty of rape and sentenced him to ten years Rigorous imprisonment.The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender.The sentence was pronounced in the State's challenge to Tejpal's acquittal by the trial court in 2021.After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda representing Tejpal sought lenient sentence for him on the grounds that he is a senior citizen today, aged 62 and that the case is a 13 year old one.Tejpal addressing the division bench of Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar said he is a "political victim" and is 62 years old and a father of two with a wife and sought a lenient sentence.He said that there is so much evidence in favour of him that he can be acquitted ten times.Solicitor general of India representing Goa Government Tushar Mehta however argued for maximum sentence for Tejpal. He urged the court to consider that Tejpal was old enough to be in a parental position vis-a vis the survivor and argued that the sentence should set a precedent and have a strong deterrent effect.Mehta said that this was not some "misunderstanding or some banter" and pointed out that Tejpal had no remorse after the incident and alleged that he repeated the same thing on the next day.He said Tejpal was brazen despite resistance and despite the survivor saying no.He further argued that the survivor's mature conduct after the incident had been wrongly portrayed as that of someone who had enjoyed the molestation."It is high time the highest constitutional court of the state gives him the maximum sentence. No means No. You may be whosoever you are but when a girl says no it means no. That deterrent message may be considered," Mehta told the court while arguing on maximum sentence for him.Mehta during the hearings seeking Tejpal's conviction argued that the survivor was a stellar witness and stood by her case and that Tejpal's apology to her was proof of what he had done. He also argued that there was no reason for a man of her father's age to send her such her the 'the fingertips' text message after midnight and that it could not reasonably have an innocent meaning. Ponda had countered that saying the 'fingertips' text message had a different context and did not prove charge of rape.He had argued that the survivor had a "propensity to lie" and that her behaviour after the alleged incident was not commensurate with someone who had been raped and traumatised.
Article Summary: Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender. After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda sought lenient sentence for him.

NEW DELHI: A seemingly innocuous WhatsApp message from a parent asking chemistry professor PV Kulkarni for his address to gift him a watch rang the first alarm-bells for CBI sleuths probing the NEET-UG paper leak. What followed was a scan of an access control app used in residential societies (Mygate) and analysis of a WhatsApp group named 'Fifa world cup', which helped the agency trace the students who bought papers and ultimately the question setters who leaked them.The chargesheet filed by CBI revealed that Mygate app logs confirmed the presence of students in the apartment of the arrested accused Kulkarni. The logs matched mobile logs, corroborating their location.Kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by NTA for NEET-UG 2026 - the medical entrance exam being cancelled on May 3 due to a paper leak. The test was reconducted on June 21.Though sworn to secrecy, Kulkarni chose to share questions with students who paid to attend "special classes" he conducted in his apartment just before the exam, the agency said in the chargesheet.His greed put paid to measures that NTA had taken to plug vulnerabilities in the logistics chain that were exploited by an organised gang.The testing agency had not factored in the possibility of subversion by a subject expert."Kulkarni and other accused paper setters would memorise or mark in a book the questions that were being set at NTA's office, later note down those questions at a hotel, and then pass these on to other accused," CBI said.The handwritten notes matched the leaked question papers. Kulkarni's seized phone contained pre-exam leaked papers in circulation and contacts with candidates, parents and co-accused. The phone contained nine images of the chemistry question paper and answer slips matching NEET-UG papers.Kulkarni, CBI said, also created a Whatsapp group called "special class" on April 25. The money, in lieu of questions, was directly collected from parents of candidates by Kulkarni or sent through co-accused Manisha Waghmare, a beautician.Nine students attended Kulkarni's classes between April 25 and 27, officials privy to investigations said. Besides, three candidates attended special classes in Latur. Eight students, who joined the WhatsApp group created by Kulkarni, and his scouts have confirmed to CBI that the leaked paper was shared with them.Kulkarni even made an attempt to get the physics paper for students, but it was leaked by another paper setter, Manisha Havaldar. She was on NTA's panel to set the physics paper and also to translate the question paper from English to Marathi and vice versa. Despite an oath of confidentiality, she allegedly leaked physics questions to the mother of a candidate for Rs 25,000 at the insistence of another accused.Eight days before the exam, Havaldar had handwritten notes of the leaked paper on her phone. She dictated the leaked paper to accused Tejas Shah for further circulation. On April 14, Shah, a member of physics faculty and chief operating officer of Abhang Prabhu Medical Academy, noted down the leaked questions dictated by Havaldar.The leaked papers also reached Rajasthan. Four days ahead of the test, 11 sets of leaked question papers were transported in a black Hyundai Verna to Jhunjhunu. The chargesheet details revealed that Mangilal Biwal and Dinesh Biwal - Sikar-based family at the core of the leak - were carrying printed material spanning the complete exam syllabus, across physics, chemistry and biology.One of the receivers, Amit, kept Class X and XII marksheets of candidates as security, and they were assured they would only need to pay if more than 150 questions matched the actual paper, CBI said.Another accused, Shivraj Motegaonkar, managing partner of RCC coaching centre, circulated leaked question papers to students, claiming these would be the "most expected" paper appearing in the exam. The night before the NEET-UG exam, a PDF file containing the question paper was leaked to 40-50 hostel students of RCC coaching students, sleuths said.On May 3, after the exam, students appeared in a video where they claimed questions predicted by Motegaonkar actually appeared in the test. The "RCC MOCK test question paper" was the leaked question paper, CBI has found.
Article Summary: PV Kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by NTA for NEET-UG 2026 - the medical entrance exam being cancelled on May 3 due to a paper leak. His greed put paid to measures that NTA had taken to plug vulnerabilities in the logistics chain.

Article Title: Government maps 27 Arunachal border locations with standard names
Article Text:
Several of the named sites on the map carry the weight of India-China conflict.

GUWAHATI/NEW DELHI: The updated Survey of India map has assigned standard place and feature names to 27 Arunachal Pradesh sites, including four mountain passes and a high-altitude lake, as part of the Union government’s strategy to remove any ambiguity on demarcation of territory and counter China’s repeated attempts to rename places on this side of the McMahon Line.The MHA said on Friday that the names were finalised in consultation with the Arunachal Pradesh government. “Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public.”Of the 27 sites identified on the map, one is a monument. Three of the rest — Longju, Maja & Bisa — are strategically important border villages in Upper Subansiri district. There are also three passes along the McMahon Line, Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La, in the same district. Thag La pass, a 1962 battleground, lies on the border in Tawang district.“These places are already marked on Indian military maps, even those of 1962 vintage. Identifying them on Survey of India maps is a bold counter to China,” a source said.Several of the named sites carry the weight of India-China conflict. Longju was one of the earliest flashpoints in the boundary dispute and was occupied by Chinese troops in 1959.Thag La overlooks Namka Chu valley, where the 1962 conflict began after Chinese forces crossed the McMahon Line.Jaswant Garh, in Tawang, commemorates Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, one of the most celebrated heroes of 1962 war. The Sher-e-Thapa Memorial in Upper Subansiri honours Hav Shere Thapa, whose resistance at Rio Bridge significantly delayed the Chinese advance in 1962. The lone lake named is Sambho Sarovar, a high-altitude glacial lake.The remaining land areas include Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun and Dhan Bari in Anjaw district; Pritnagar, Buddhamandir, Jairampur, Teritnagar and Ramnagar in Changlang; Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar and Baisakhi in West Kameng; Chhota Ropuk and Bara Ropuk in Upper Subansiri; and Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura and Kamlang Nagar in Lohit.In April, China announced Chinese names for 23 locations in Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing refers to as “South Tibet”. The external affairs ministry then said assigning “fictitious names” wouldn’t alter the reality that Arunachal Pradesh “was, is, and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India”. China has carried out similar renaming exercises periodically.McMahon Line demarcates the boundary between India and China in the eastern sector, separating Arunachal from Tibet.
Article Summary: The updated Survey of India map has assigned standard place and feature names to 27 Arunachal Pradesh sites. The names are part of the Union government’s strategy to remove any ambiguity on demarcation of territory. China has repeated attempts to rename places on this side of the McMahon Line.

Article Title: 'Fake news, AI-generated': MEA dismisses report of India requesting defence pact with Israel after Mecca agreement

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday rejected a report claiming India had approached Israel for a defence pact following the signing of a new security agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey. The ministry called the claim “fake news” generated using artificial intelligence.The report, published by Turkish outlet Straturka and subsequently circulated on social media, claimed that New Delhi had initiated discussions with Tel Aviv to counter the emerging Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security arrangement. The report cited unnamed Pakistani sources.The MEA’s Fact Check unit shared a screenshot of the report on X and flagged it as fake, warning users against what it described as malicious social media posts created using AI.“We caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms which use AI to create fake content!” the ministry’s Fact Check wing said.The claim surfaced after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to deepen military and security cooperation among the three countries. Pakistan has described the agreement as a collective-deterrence arrangement, with its foreign ministry saying an armed attack on any one of the three signatories would be treated as an attack on all three.The agreement has drawn attention in New Delhi, with the MEA saying India is closely monitoring developments.“We are also closely following this development, and we shall keep you updated,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at the ministry’s weekly briefing.The MEA’s clarification came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by phone with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership and reviewed cooperation between the two countries across several areas.The conversation focused on strengthening bilateral ties and the existing partnership between India and Israel, rather than any new defence pact linked to the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey agreement.

Article Title: Air India salary hikes salaries of pilots by up to 15%
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and increases tapering by rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will get command upgrades in AI Express, which has single-aisle aircraft, then move to AI, which has wide-body aircraft with higher pay, to build progression within the group. Air India has tried to make Air India Express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the B737 fleet.Air India pilots have for years been facing a 40-hour guaranteed pay — meaning they get minimum pay for these hours irrespective of actual flying, while flying more means more pay — while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. Under the revised framework, Air India will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Rates beyond 40 hours have been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month. Pakistan airspace closure means longer routes, higher flying time and greater pilot requirements.A senior commander flying 55 hours a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh, while a first officer will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh.Privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24 days, though weekly offs will not be counted as leave.Since Tata Group took over Air India and Air India Express in Jan 2022, it has grown from around 100 to 300 aircraft. Under the new framework, Air India Express will serve as the “primary pathway” for command upgrades. They can then progress to Air India for wide-body flying. A fleet allowance is being offered to pilots supporting the B737 fleet in Air India Express.
Article Summary: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and increases tapering by rank. First officers or co-pilots will get command upgrades in AI Express, then move to AI, which has wide-body aircraft with higher pay. Air India has tried to make Air India Express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the B737 fleet.

NEW DELHI: Barely six months after appointing a sessions judge to exclusively hear coal scam cases in Delhi, Supreme Court has replaced her, acting on an unusual request from the Delhi high court, which said she and another special CBI judge were “better suited for certain other responsibilities”.A bench of Chief Justice Suryakant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana, in an order, recorded that Delhi high court had sought the transfer of special judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor so they could be assigned other responsibilities.Sharma had assumed charge in January after SC approved Delhi HC’s request to relieve then incumbent Sanjay Bansal, who had presided over the special coal scam court for nearly four-and-a-half years. Mor was appointed special judge in April 2025. The latest request came with Sharma barely six months into her tenure and Mor having completed just over a year in the post.SC noted that it had received a letter from the registrar general of Delhi HC stating that Sharma and Mor were “better suited for certain other responsibilities”. The HC also described both judicial officers as “of outstanding merit” and said it wished to utilise their services elsewhere.Accepting the request, the top court permitted Delhi high court to transfer Sharma and Mor from the posts of special judges hearing CBI coal scam cases. It also approved the appointment of Virender Kumar Kharta, earlier special judge of the NDPS court at Saket, and Ajay Garg, previously an additional sessions judge at a fast-track court in Tis Hazari, as their replacements. Kharta will succeed Sharma, while Garg will take over from Mor.On Friday, Delhi HC issued the consequential transfer and posting orders. Interestingly, neither Sharma nor Mor has been assigned a fresh judicial posting. According to the notification, both have been attached to the office of the principal district and sessions judge (CBI).The high court directed both officers to notify all matters in which judgments or orders had been reserved before relinquishing charge and pronounce them on the scheduled date or, at the latest, within two to three weeks despite the transfer. The dates fixed for pronouncement must also be reflected in the cause lists of both the previous and new courts, as well as on the court’s website.Last year, 29 CBI corruption cases were pending before two special coal scam courts, while more than 27 had already been disposed of.
Article Summary: Delhi high court had sought the transfer of special judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor so they could be assigned other responsibilities. Sharma assumed charge in January after SC approved Delhi HC’s request to relieve then incumbent Sanjay Bansal, who had presided over the special coal scam court for nearly four-and-a-half years.

NEW DELHI: In another round of diplomatic engagement on the border issue, India and China had “frank discussions” and reviewed the situation along the line of actual control (LAC), with the former underlining that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the development of bilateral relations.The Indian side also reiterated the need for early convening of the next meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers, which was established in 2006, and emphasised the importance of sharing technical details on upstream projects.Following the recent announcement of a mega dam project by China, India has been raising the need for transparency and consultation with downstream countries on such upstream activities.According to the Indian govt, as a lower riparian state with established user rights to the waters of trans-border rivers, India routinely conveys its views and concerns to the Chinese authorities, and has urged them to ensure that the interests of downstream states are not harmed by activities in upstream areas. Article Title: Supreme Court seeks Bihar minister's record of appointment & nomination as MLC
Article Text:
With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved; Samrat Choudhary's council, constituted on May 7, included Prakash

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday sought records from the Bihar government relating to the appointment of Deepak Prakash, who was not a member of the assembly, as a minister in Nov last year, his re-induction into the cabinet in May and his recent hurried nomination as an MLC allegedly to skirt around the six-month deadline within which such a minister must get elected to the House.A PIL has challenged his continuance as minister after the expiry of the six-month deadline within which a person, who is not a member of the assembly or legislative council, must get elected as a member of either house.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, for the Bihar government, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi, and V Mohana that the minister has since been nominated as an MLC by the governor; hence, his continuance was not unconstitutional.However, the petitioner, relying on the SC's 2001 judgment in the SR Chaudhari case, which had categorically stated that the six-month deadline was non-negotiable, said the six-month deadline expired on May 20. With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved. The new council of ministers was constituted under Samrat Choudhary on May 7, which included Prakash. The bench asked the Bihar government to place on record all documents relating to the appointment of Prakash in the first instance, his re-induction and subsequent nomination as MLC.In its 2001 judgment by a three-judge bench, SC had ruled, "Permitting a non-legislator minister to be re-appointed, without getting elected within the period prescribed by Article 164(4) (six months), would amount to ignoring the electorate in having its say as to who should represent it - a position which is wholly unacceptable."The seductive temptations to cling to office regardless of constitutional restraint must be totally eschewed. Will of the people cannot be permitted to be subordinated to political expediency of the prime minister or the chief minister as the case may be, to have in his cabinet a non-legislator as a minister for an indefinite period by repeated re-appointments without the individual seeking popular mandate of the electorate. "The SC added, "Chief ministers or governors must... not sacrifice either political responsibility or parliamentary conventions at the altar of political expediency."
Article Summary: Deepak Prakash, who was not a member of the assembly, as a minister in Nov last year. PIL has challenged his continuance as minister after the expiry of the six-month deadline. With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved. Samrat Choudhary's council, constituted on May 7, included P Rakash.

She had sought the quashing of the proceedings and protection from any coercive action by the police.Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya of the Calcutta high court had directed Moitra to appear before the investigating officer on August 14 for questioning and ordered that no coercive steps be taken against her until October 5, subject to her complying with the investigation.The high court had noted that the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita invoked against Moitra carry a maximum punishment of less than seven years, making her eligible for protection from coercive action as long as she cooperates with the probe.The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the high court again on October 1.
Article Summary: Supreme Court refuses to entertain Mahua Moitra's plea against a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police. Article Title: No conflict of interest in RDI Fund, says government

NEW DELHI: The government on Friday said the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund is being implemented through a robust institutional framework with "stringent conflict-of-interest safeguards" in place, highlighting that it is designed "not to exclude domain expertise but to regulate it through clearly defined conflict-of-interest provisions".Rebutting a media report that 15 of the 22 entities that got public funds to boost India's deep-tech ambitions have investment links to seven members of the selection committee, raising questions of conflict of interest and propriety, Technology Development Board (TDB) secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said the mere existence of a professional or investment association with an innovation ecosystem entity does not constitute a violation of conflict-of-interest norms."What the framework requires is full disclosure of such interests and complete recusal from the evaluation and decision-making process relating to the proposal concerned... All members had, accordingly, recused themselves, and each decision was taken not by simple majority but by super-majority (two-thirds) of eligible members," said Pathak."Members who declare a conflict of interest neither participate in discussions nor vote on the concerned proposal."Pathak also underlined that TDB has "consistently followed similar conflict-of-interest safeguards for nearly three decades" while supporting indigenous technology development.Since its establishment under an Act of Parliament in 1996, TDB has relied upon independent expert committees rather than individual officials for evaluating technology proposals.The same institutional principles continue to govern project selection under the RDI Fund, reinforcing continuity, credibility and public confidence in the decision-making process, he added.Prof Umesh V Waghmare, secretary in the department of science and technology and TDB chairperson, said the government has followed the conflict-of-interest guidelines and framework diligently and strongly believes that there have been no violations. TDB is one of the agencies selected to grant money under the Centre's Rs 1 lakh crore RDI Fund. It has, so far, approved assistance for 22 projects involving Rs 2,192 crore of financing.

NEW DELHI: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms, "which are offensive to moral standards of society", without infringing upon the rights and freedom of individuals.The department-related standing committee on the ministry of home affairs, in its recommendations in the 259th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, said the proposed comprehensive statutory framework for regulating OTT content must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.While observing that the existing framework continued to rely largely on self-regulation by OTT platforms, the committee - in its recommendations on the action taken on its 254th report - reiterated that the government examine the feasibility of establishing an independent post-release review panel - comprising experts from fields like child development, education, law, social sciences and civil society - to review flagged OTT content and lay down appropriate corrective measures.The panel had, in its 254th report, said, "OTT platforms have emerged as a primary source of entertainment in India, with a reach that surpasses traditional cinema, including a substantial audience of minors." The committee pointed out that unlike films, which require mandatory pre-certification under the Cinematograph Act, OTT content operates under a self-classification system with post-release grievance redressal as per the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.The panel said that although the aforesaid rules require age ratings, parental controls and a grievance mechanism, the lack of pre-release checks and weak age verification still leaves minors exposed to harmful content. Accordingly, it recommended that the government consider establishing a recognised panel of experts who will monitor new OTT releases.It suggested that the post-release review panel watch the flagged or trending content based on user complaints submitted through a standardised grievance mechanism.The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines "keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country". It recommended that the panel also work out suitable penalties for infringement of these norms/guidelines.
Article Summary: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms. The proposed framework must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.

NEW DELHI: A new paper by NCAER has proposed lifting prohibition in Bihar to generate resources for financing development and capital expenditure. It argued prohibition has not reduced crime against women and legal drinking has shifted to the consumption of illegal alcohol and drugs.The paper by a team of economists led by Ratna Sahay said an end to prohibition can help the state increase its tax revenue by 14-15% while reducing expenditure on enforcement. To achieve its goals, it suggested higher capex, lower subsidies, raising resources and getting more resources from the Centre.It noted that Bihar's debt burden at 39% of state GDP is higher than both high- and low-income groups, with the exception of Punjab (47%) and Bengal, which is similar. "Raising state revenues is insufficient to finance the reforms, given the state's limited taxing capacity. Additional transfers from the Centre are needed, depending on the reform," the paper said.

Article Title: India’s crude import bill up 26% in ’26-27 Q1 despite 18% volume fall
Article Text:
Russia, India's biggest supplier during the quarter, supplied crude at an average cost of $2,408 per tonne, while UAE crude cost $2,213 per tonne

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's crude import bill rose 26% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026-27, despite volumes falling 18%, as the West Asia conflict disrupted supplies and pushed up oil prices.Commerce department data showed India imported 59.7 million tonnes (MT) of crude between April and June this year, down from 73 MT in the corresponding period last fiscal. Import bill, however, rose to $49 billion from $39 billion in April-June 2025.India is the world's third-largest crude importer, with imports meeting 88% of annual consumption. Global oil prices, which were below $70 per barrel before the US-Iran conflict broke out in Feb, surged after shipments through the Strait of Hormuz - which handles a fifth of global oil transit - were disrupted. Around 40% of India's crude imports came through the strait from West Asian suppliers. Brent crude touched nearly $120 per barrel at the conflict's peak. The weakening rupee also added to the import bill.Since India imports 1.8-2 billion barrels of crude a year, every $1-per-barrel increase in oil prices can add up to $2 billion to its oil import bill.Average cost of crude sourced from different countries varied, partly because of differences in freight, insurance and war-risk premiums.Russia, India's biggest supplier during the quarter, supplied crude at an average cost of $2,408 per tonne, while UAE crude cost $2,213 per tonne."Our priority at that time was to secure supplies from wherever possible to ensure energy security for 1.4 billion people," said an executive of a state-run refining company, adding that discounts available before the conflict had disappeared and refiners were forced to pay hefty war-risk premiums.Russia remained India's top crude supplier in the first quarter of FY27, accounting for more than 40% of imports. UAE (14.6%), Saudi Arabia (9.9%), Venezuela (5.2%) and Oman (4.5%) were the other major suppliers.
Article Summary: India is the world's third-largest crude importer, with imports meeting 88% of annual consumption. Russia remained India's top crude supplier in the first quarter of FY27, accounting for more than 40% of imports. No terror angle had emerged in the probe so far, a police spokesperson said. The investigation officer and district mobile forensic unit collected evidence from the scene. Further investigation was underway.
